brief: Ganaka the knotted-cord spirit tying knots in a long cord with great pride, a row of old palm leaves laid out on a low table; Dādī laughing; Śuka counting on his claws; lamplight.

The inner room of the village school library at morning: the Ācārya unlocking a carved door; high on a shelf a small grey spirit made of knotted cords and pebbles pointing at rows of books and muttering; Dādī and Śuka looking up at it; sunbeams full of dust.

The ghat steps full of morning life: a boy reading, a girl singing, a boatman resting beside his boat, a heron in the shallows; the small grey-blue spirit sweeping his arm over the scene while Dādī asks a question.

Dawn on the stone ghat steps of a calm river: people bathing, a boy reading on the steps, and on the lowest step a small grey-blue spirit like river mist with his feet in the water, pointing; you, Dādī and Śuka coming down the steps.
Dādī pointing first at a boy on the ghat steps and then at the small grey-blue spirit, as though introducing them; Śuka looking from one to the other; calm river light.
The boat on a widening river with you, Dādī with her pen, Śuka on the awning and the boatman, the small boat-shaped spirit circling the boat; Dādī lifting one finger as if teaching.

Deep in the grove at night: a single tiny golden spark flickering on and off in the dark with a thin trail of smoke; the Vetāla seated on a root watching it with a gentle expression; you, Dādī and Śuka kneeling to look; ancient gnarled trunks around.

The very edge of the old grove at night: four ancient grey spirits seated in a half-circle, faint and wise, like carved figures worn smooth by time; the Vetāla introducing them with an open hand; you, Dādī and Śuka standing respectfully in front.
